_note_scope: Tracked and shared. settings.json is read for the launch directory and does not cascade from subdirectories — fine here, because there is exactly one launch point (the workspace root). Per-machine deltas belong in .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored), the ONLY local settings file Claude Code reads. Every local entry carries a _note with its consequence and date.
_note_env: Env vars set here are inherited by every child process, including probe sessions. Any env var added MUST carry its own _note stating what behaviour it changes and the date — an unnoted switch is a trap with a timer on it (measured 2026-08-02, Claude Code 2.1.220: an unnoted env var silently changed --add-dir behaviour).
_note_paths: Both hook commands below resolve their script through $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR — the directory claude was launched from, confirmed set for hook processes (measured 2026-08-16, Claude Code 2.1.233). No absolute path in this file points into the tree, so the tree can live anywhere.
_note_env_todo_tools: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 (2026-08-27): turns on task-tracking tools, which Claude Code 2.1.248 gates off by default. Subagents can only ever subset the parent session's tool surface, so without this NO agent def can grant a todo tool, whatever its tools: key says. Revert by deleting the key.
_note_env_tool_search: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=1 (2026-08-27): keeps rarely-used tools DEFERRED — name only in context, full schema fetched on demand. The cost of a tool is its schema; deferral removes that cost without removing the tool. Pinned explicitly so it does not silently flip.
_note_permissions: Deny-only, deliberately. Rule 4 marks p.* files as the owner's and read-only; until 2026-08-27 that was prose asking a model to behave. ONLY Edit(path) RULES WORK: the harness prints a startup warning that Write(...) and NotebookEdit(...) path rules 'are not matched by file permission checks' — an Edit rule already covers every file-editing tool. Do not add a Write(...) path rule for anything. KNOWN HOLE, half-closed: sessions that run bash-first make `sed -i p.foo.md` a Bash call, which no Edit rule sees — that half is the readonly_guard PreToolUse hook above, the same rung the gitlink guard sits on. rm -rf scoping is the same shape: a permission rule matches a command prefix, not a resolved path, so 'destructive outside the workspace' is not expressible here.
_note_sessionend: SessionEnd: runs check-digest in the BACKGROUND (setsid nohup) so exit is never blocked by a model call; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is inherited by the hook process, which is how the digest knows which session ended. /wrap also runs it, in the foreground; the digest is idempotent per session so both firing is harmless. The objective side of memory is a process, not an agent.
